learning_outcomes.text: Competence in the sustainable use of resources and in the prevention of negative impacts on the natural and social environment.
That students have developed the necessary learning skills to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to apply knowledge in practice.
Ability to use computer science fluently at user level.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases, and computer programs with application in engineering.
Be able to apply basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers.
Be able to apply basic knowledge about operating systems.
Be able to apply basic knowledge about databases.
Be able to apply basic knowledge about computer programs with application in engineering.

syllabus_topics: Theory. Module 1: The computer. Definitions. Basic computer operation. The central computer and peripherals.
Theory. Module 2: Software. Operating systems. Programming languages. Databases. Applications.

Theory. Module 3: Fundamentals of programming. Introduction to the software life cycle. Algorithm: concept, elements, and representation. Structured programming. Top-down design. Study of a programming language.
Practice. Module 1: Program development: primitive data types, variables, constants and operators, selection and iteration statements, top-down design, arrays and files.
Practice. Module 2: Use of computer applications in engineering.
teaching_methods: Non-contact learning activities (individual study and autonomous work on the course contents by understanding theoretical concepts and solving programming exercises)
Tutorial activities (personal attention to the student to advise them on various aspects of the course development)
Evaluation activities (assessment tests on the various course contents)
Computer practicals (problem-based learning for algorithm design, programming exercises, database creation and operations)
Theory (expository method/lecture for theoretical units, partial progress tests, doubt resolution, and past exam exercises)
